name: Macau
tagline: Portuguese lanes, temples and neon casinos
summary: A Portuguese colony for over 400 years, Macau mixes cobbled squares, Baroque churches and Chinese temples in a World Heritage old town, with giant casino resorts on the reclaimed Cotai strip. Its Macanese food, a blend of Portuguese and Cantonese cooking, is one of Asia's oldest fusion cuisines.
seasonNote: October to December is dry and comfortable. Summer is hot, humid and typhoon-prone. Chinese New Year and Golden Week (early October) are very crowded; the Grand Prix is in November.
arrival: Ferries run from Hong Kong (about one hour) and the Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macau Bridge buses take 45 minutes from Hong Kong Airport. Macau has its own airport, and many nationalities get visa-free entry.
gettingAround: Free casino shuttle buses link the ferry terminals and hotels; the light rail runs to Taipa and Cotai, and the old town is walkable.
cashTip: The pataca is used alongside the Hong Kong dollar, which is accepted almost everywhere at par; change is often given in patacas.
foodTip: Portuguese egg tarts, pork chop buns, African chicken and minchi, and almond cookies.
buyTip: Almond cookies, beef jerky, Portuguese tiles and wine.
baseArea: Old town near Senado Square or a Cotai resort

connections.note: TurboJET and Cotai Water Jet ferries, or buses over the bridge.

items.name: Ruins of St Paul's
items.summary: The carved stone façade of a 17th-century Jesuit church, all that survived a fire.
items.expect: Free; very crowded in the middle of the day.
items.tip: Come early morning or after dark when it is lit.

items.name: Senado Square
items.summary: A wave-patterned Portuguese square lined with pastel colonial buildings.
items.expect: The heart of the Historic Centre.
items.tip: Walk on to St Dominic's Church.

items.name: Monte Fort and Macao Museum
items.summary: A Jesuit fort with cannons over the city, holding the city museum.
items.expect: Next to St Paul's.
items.tip: Visit the museum for Macau's story.
items.why: Views and history in one stop.

items.name: A-Ma Temple
items.summary: A temple to the sea goddess, older than the city; Macau's name comes from it.
items.expect: Incense coils and shrines climbing a hillside.
items.tip: Go in the morning when locals pray.

items.name: Macau Tower
items.summary: A 338 m tower with an observation deck and the world's highest commercial bungee jump.
items.expect: Tickets for the deck; separate fees for adventures.
items.tip: Go at sunset.
items.why: Views over Macau and the Pearl River.

items.name: Taipa Village
items.summary: Lanes of old shophouses, Portuguese restaurants and the Taipa Houses Museum.
items.expect: Busy with snack stalls on Rua do Cunha.
items.tip: Walk to the Taipa Houses by the old waterfront.

items.name: Cotai Strip
items.summary: A row of giant casino resorts with shows, shopping and replica landmarks.
items.expect: Free to walk through; dress smart for casinos.
items.tip: See the light shows after dark.

items.name: Portuguese egg tarts
items.summary: Flaky tarts with a caramelised custard top, famous at Lord Stow's in Coloane.
items.expect: Best warm from the oven.
items.tip: Buy a few to eat straight away.

items.name: Pork chop bun
items.summary: A marinated fried pork chop in a crisp bun.
items.expect: Queues at the famous stalls in Taipa.
items.tip: Eat it hot.

items.name: Macanese cooking
items.summary: African chicken, minchi minced meat and curry crab, a mix of Portuguese, African and Cantonese.
items.expect: Small family restaurants in the old town.
items.tip: Order minchi; it's the home-cooked classic.
items.why: One of the world's first fusion cuisines.

name: Bali · South coast
summary: Bali's south coast is where most trips begin: the cafés and beach clubs of Seminyak and Canggu, the surf breaks and cliffs of Uluwatu, and seafood on the sand at Jimbaran. Hindu temples like Uluwatu and Tanah Lot stand over the sea, and Ubud's rice terraces are an hour inland.
seasonNote: April to October is the dry season; July and August and Christmas are the busiest. November to March is wet, with short heavy showers. Nyepi, the day of silence in March, closes the whole island, including the airport.
arrival: Fly into Ngurah Rai International Airport (Denpasar), 15 to 45 minutes from the south-coast areas. Pay the Bali tourist levy online before you arrive, and check visa-on-arrival rules.
gettingAround: Traffic is slow; use ride-hailing apps (Grab, Gojek), a private driver for day trips, or a scooter if you are experienced.
cashTip: Carry rupiah for warungs and temple donations; cards work in cafés and hotels. Use bank ATMs inside buildings.
foodTip: Babi guling (spit-roast pork), nasi campur, satay lilit and seafood on the beach at Jimbaran.
buyTip: Sarongs, silver from Celuk, woven bags and coffee.

connections.note: By car or ride-hailing; traffic varies.

items.name: Uluwatu Temple
items.summary: A sea temple on a 70 m cliff, with the Kecak fire dance at sunset.
items.expect: Sarongs are lent at the gate; monkeys snatch glasses and phones.
items.tip: Book the sunset Kecak dance and hold on to your belongings.

items.name: Tanah Lot
items.summary: A temple on a rock in the sea, reachable on foot at low tide.
items.expect: Very busy at sunset.
items.tip: Go at low tide to reach the base.

items.name: Seminyak beach
items.summary: A long sandy beach lined with beach clubs and sunset bars.
items.expect: Strong currents; swim between the flags.
items.tip: Grab a beanbag on the sand at sunset.

items.name: Padang Padang Beach
items.summary: A small beach reached through a rock cleft, with a famous surf break.
items.expect: Steep steps down; small entry fee.
items.tip: Come in the morning before it fills.
items.why: The prettiest beach on the Bukit.

items.name: Garuda Wisnu Kencana
items.summary: A giant 121 m statue of Vishnu riding Garuda in a cultural park.
items.expect: Dance shows run through the day.
items.tip: Combine with Uluwatu in the afternoon.
items.why: One of the world's tallest statues.

items.name: Canggu
items.summary: Rice-field lanes, surf beaches and Bali's busiest café scene.
items.expect: Popular with digital nomads.
items.tip: Watch sunset at Echo Beach.

items.name: Nusa Penida
items.summary: An island of towering cliffs, Kelingking Beach and manta-ray snorkelling.
items.expect: A fast boat from Sanur takes 45 minutes; roads are rough.
items.tip: Book a driver on the island and start early.

items.name: Babi guling
items.summary: Spit-roast suckling pork with spiced rice, crackling and sausage.
items.expect: Usually sold out by early afternoon.
items.tip: Go for lunch, not dinner.

items.name: Jimbaran seafood
items.summary: Grilled fish, prawns and lobster at tables on the sand at sunset.
items.expect: Seafood is priced by weight.
items.tip: Agree the price before it is cooked.
items.why: Dinner with your toes in the sand.

items.name: Nasi campur at a warung
items.summary: Rice with a choice of small dishes from a counter at a local warung.
items.expect: Cheap and quick.
items.tip: Point at what looks good.

name: Doha
summary: Qatar's capital curves around a bay of glittering towers. It has world-class museums, including I. M. Pei's Museum of Islamic Art and the desert-rose National Museum, a lively rebuilt souq, and dunes that run down to an inland sea in the south.
seasonNote: November to March is warm and pleasant. April and October are hot; May to September is extremely hot and humid. Ramadan changes opening hours, and eating in public by day is discouraged.
arrival: Hamad International Airport is 20 minutes from the centre by metro or taxi; Doha is a major stopover hub, and many nationalities get visa-free entry.
gettingAround: The Doha Metro is cheap and clean; taxis and ride-hailing cover the rest.
cashTip: Cards work almost everywhere; carry some riyals for the souq.
foodTip: Machboos (spiced rice with meat), luqaimat dumplings with date syrup, and karak tea.
buyTip: Dates, oud perfume, spices and falconry gear at Souq Waqif.
baseArea: West Bay, Msheireb or near Souq Waqif

items.name: Museum of Islamic Art
items.summary: I. M. Pei's geometric museum of 1,400 years of Islamic art, with views of the skyline.
items.expect: Free for residents; a fee for visitors.
items.tip: Stay for the park and skyline view at sunset.
items.why: One of the world's great museums.

items.name: National Museum of Qatar
items.summary: Jean Nouvel's building of interlocking discs, inspired by the desert rose.
items.expect: Immersive films tell Qatar's story.
items.tip: Allow two hours.
items.why: The architecture alone is worth it.

items.name: Souq Waqif
items.summary: A restored market of spice stalls, falcon shops and cafés.
items.expect: Comes alive in the evening; dress modestly.
items.tip: Visit the falcon souq and hospital nearby.

items.name: Doha Corniche
items.summary: A 7 km waterfront promenade facing the West Bay towers.
items.expect: Dhow boats offer short cruises.
items.tip: Take a dhow cruise at sunset.

items.name: Katara Cultural Village
items.summary: A cultural district with an amphitheatre, mosques, galleries and a beach.
items.expect: Free to wander.
items.tip: See the pigeon towers and the golden mosque.
items.why: Arts and architecture in one place.

items.name: The Pearl
items.summary: An artificial island of marinas, Mediterranean-style piazzas and cafés.
items.expect: Upmarket shops and restaurants.
items.tip: Walk Qanat Quartier's colourful canals.

items.name: Khor Al Adaid (Inland Sea)
items.summary: Giant dunes rolling down to a sea inlet on the Saudi border.
items.expect: Only reachable by 4x4; book a tour with dune bashing.
items.tip: Go in the afternoon and stay for sunset.

items.name: Machboos
items.summary: Spiced rice with chicken, lamb or fish, the Gulf's national dish.
items.expect: Served on large platters.
items.tip: Try it with Qatari-style tomato sauce.

items.name: Luqaimat
items.summary: Crisp fried dough balls drizzled with date syrup.
items.expect: Sold hot at souq stalls.
items.tip: Eat them immediately.

items.name: Karak tea
items.summary: Strong spiced milk tea sold at roadside cafés across the city.
items.expect: Very cheap and very sweet.
items.tip: Pair it with a chapati wrap.

name: Abu Dhabi
tagline: A grand mosque, a Louvre and island beaches
summary: The UAE's capital spreads across islands on the Gulf. The white marble Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque is one of the world's largest and most beautiful, the Louvre Abu Dhabi floats under a lattice dome on Saadiyat Island, and Yas Island has theme parks and the Formula 1 circuit.
seasonNote: November to March is warm and sunny. May to September is extremely hot. The Formula 1 Grand Prix is in late November or December. Ramadan changes opening hours.
arrival: Zayed International Airport is 30 minutes from the city. Buses and cars reach Dubai in about 90 minutes.
gettingAround: Taxis are cheap and plentiful; free shuttles run between some Saadiyat and Yas sights.
cashTip: Cards work everywhere; carry a few dirhams for small shops.
foodTip: Emirati dishes like machboos and harees, luqaimat, shawarma, and Arabic coffee with dates.
buyTip: Dates, Arabic perfume, carpets and gold.
baseArea: Corniche, Saadiyat Island or Yas Island

items.name: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
items.summary: A vast white marble mosque with 82 domes, crystal chandeliers and the world's largest hand-knotted carpet.
items.expect: Free and open to visitors of all faiths outside prayer times; book a slot online. Modest dress, with headscarves for women; closed to tourists on Friday mornings.
items.tip: Come late afternoon and stay as it lights up at dusk.
items.why: One of the world's most beautiful mosques.

items.name: Louvre Abu Dhabi
items.summary: A museum of world art under a lattice dome that scatters a 'rain of light'.
items.expect: Galleries run from ancient times to today.
items.tip: Leave time to sit under the dome by the water.

items.name: Qasr Al Watan
items.summary: The working presidential palace, with domed halls of white granite.
items.expect: An evening light show runs on the façade.
items.tip: Stay for the light and sound show.

items.name: Qasr Al Hosn
items.summary: The city's oldest stone building, an 18th-century fort.
items.expect: A museum of Abu Dhabi's story.
items.tip: Pair with the House of Artisans next door.

items.name: Mangrove National Park
items.summary: Calm mangrove channels to explore by kayak.
items.expect: Guided kayak tours leave from the Eastern Mangroves.
items.tip: Go at sunrise or sunset.
items.why: Nature in the middle of the city.

items.name: Saadiyat Beach
items.summary: A long white beach where turtles nest and the water is calm.
items.expect: Public beach with a small fee.
items.tip: Visit with the Louvre on the same day.
items.why: One of the Gulf's best beaches.

items.name: Yas Island
items.summary: Ferrari World, Warner Bros. World, Yas Waterworld and the Formula 1 circuit.
items.expect: Big ticket prices; combo tickets save money.
items.tip: Ride Formula Rossa, one of the world's fastest coasters.

items.name: Emirati cooking
items.summary: Machboos, harees and balaleet in a traditional Emirati restaurant.
items.expect: Few restaurants serve it; look for heritage cafés.
items.tip: Try balaleet, sweet vermicelli with egg, for breakfast.
items.why: The local food most visitors miss.

items.name: Shawarma
items.summary: Spit-roasted chicken or lamb wrapped with garlic sauce and pickles.
items.expect: Cheap at cafeterias everywhere.
items.tip: Order a chicken shawarma with extra toum.

items.name: Arabic coffee and dates
items.summary: Light, cardamom-spiced coffee in tiny cups with dates.
items.expect: Offered as a welcome in many places.
items.tip: Shake the cup gently when you've had enough.

name: Penang · George Town
tagline: Street art, clan houses and Malaysia's best street food
summary: George Town, on Penang island, is a World Heritage port of shophouses, clan temples, mosques and Hindu shrines side by side. Its street art and murals draw walkers, and its hawker food, from char kway teow to assam laksa, is famous across Asia.
seasonNote: December to March is the driest. It is hot and humid all year, with afternoon storms from April to November. Chinese New Year and Thaipusam bring big festivals.
arrival: Penang International Airport is 30 minutes from George Town. Trains from Kuala Lumpur reach Butterworth in about 4 hours, then a ferry crosses to the island.
gettingAround: The heritage core is walkable; Grab is cheap, and the free CAT bus loops the old town.
cashTip: Carry ringgit for hawker stalls; cards work in cafés and hotels.
foodTip: Char kway teow, assam laksa, nasi kandar and cendol from hawker stalls.
buyTip: Nyonya kebaya, beaded slippers, tau sar pneah pastries and white coffee.

connections.note: Or about 4 hours by train to Butterworth.

items.name: Street art of Armenian Street
items.summary: Murals and iron caricatures around old lanes, led by Ernest Zacharevic's 'Kids on Bicycle'.
items.expect: Pick up a mural map; very hot by midday.
items.tip: Walk early morning to avoid queues for photos.

items.name: Khoo Kongsi
items.summary: An ornate clan temple of carved beams and gilded shrines.
items.expect: Small entry fee; quiet courtyard.
items.tip: Read about the clan system in the small museum.

items.name: Cheong Fatt Tze Mansion
items.summary: The Blue Mansion of a 19th-century tycoon, restored with feng shui courtyards.
items.expect: Guided tours only, a few times a day.
items.tip: Book a tour time in advance.

items.name: Clan Jetties
items.summary: Wooden stilt villages over the water, each built by one Chinese clan.
items.expect: Homes are lived in; respect privacy.
items.tip: Visit at sunset at the end of Chew Jetty.

items.name: Kek Lok Si Temple
items.summary: One of Southeast Asia's largest Buddhist temples, with a pagoda and a giant Guanyin statue.
items.expect: Lit up with lanterns at Chinese New Year.
items.tip: Take the inclined lift to the statue.

items.name: Penang Hill
items.summary: A funicular climb to cool air and views over George Town.
items.expect: Queues at weekends.
items.tip: Go up late afternoon and stay for the lights.
items.why: The best view on the island.

items.name: Fort Cornwallis
items.summary: The star-shaped fort where Francis Light landed in 1786.
items.expect: Small and quick.
items.tip: Walk along the Esplanade afterwards.

items.name: Char kway teow
items.summary: Flat rice noodles fried over high heat with prawns, cockles and egg.
items.expect: Look for stalls with a queue.
items.tip: Ask for it with duck egg.

items.name: Assam laksa
items.summary: Sour tamarind fish soup with thick noodles, mint and pineapple.
items.expect: Gurney Drive hawker centre is the classic spot.
items.tip: Add the shrimp paste.

items.name: Nasi kandar
items.summary: Rice flooded with mixed curries, from Tamil-Muslim kitchens open day and night.
items.expect: Point at curries; ask for 'kuah campur'.
items.tip: Go to a famous 24-hour shop late at night.

name: Jeju Island
tagline: Volcanic peaks, lava caves and sea women
summary: Korea's holiday island is a volcano rising from the sea. Its World Heritage sights include the crater of Seongsan Ilchulbong, the Manjanggul lava tube and Hallasan, the country's highest peak, while haenyeo women still free-dive for shellfish along the black-rock coast.
seasonNote: Spring brings canola flowers and cherry blossoms; autumn is clear and good for hiking. July and August are hot, humid and busy, with typhoons possible. Winter is windy but mild.
arrival: Fly to Jeju from Seoul (about 1 hour; one of the world's busiest routes) or Busan. Many nationalities can visit Jeju visa-free.
gettingAround: Renting a car is easiest; island buses work but are slow.
cashTip: Cards work almost everywhere; carry a little cash for markets.
foodTip: Black pork barbecue, abalone porridge, hairtail fish and hallabong tangerines.
buyTip: Hallabong products, green tea from O'sulloc and dol hareubang stone figures.

connections.note: Flights every few minutes from Gimpo.

items.name: Seongsan Ilchulbong
items.summary: A tuff cone crater rising from the sea, climbed for sunrise.
items.expect: A 30-minute climb with many stairs.
items.tip: Go at sunrise, then watch the haenyeo dive below.

items.name: Hallasan
items.summary: South Korea's highest mountain, with a crater lake at the summit.
items.expect: Summit trails need booking ahead and a very early start.
items.tip: Take the Yeongsil trail for a shorter scenic hike.

items.name: Manjanggul Lava Tube
items.summary: A lava tunnel over 7 km long, with a 1 km section open to walk.
items.expect: Cool and wet inside year round.
items.tip: Bring a jacket.
items.why: One of the world's finest lava tubes.

items.name: Haenyeo divers
items.summary: Jeju's women divers, some in their 80s, who free-dive for shellfish.
items.expect: Short shows near Seongsan; their catch is sold fresh.
items.tip: Visit the Haenyeo Museum in Gujwa too.

items.name: Jusangjeolli Cliff
items.summary: Hexagonal basalt columns where waves crash on the south coast.
items.expect: A short walk from the car park.
items.tip: Visit on a windy day for big waves.

items.name: Cheonjiyeon Falls
items.summary: A waterfall in a lush gorge, lit up in the evening.
items.expect: An easy path; open until late.
items.tip: Go after dark.

items.name: Udo Island
items.summary: A small island of white beaches, peanut ice cream and coastal cycling.
items.expect: A 15-minute ferry from Seongsan.
items.tip: Rent an e-bike to loop the island.

items.name: Black pork barbecue
items.summary: Thick slices of Jeju black pig grilled at your table, dipped in anchovy sauce.
items.expect: Busy black pork streets in Jeju City and Seogwipo.
items.tip: Order the ogyeopsal (skin-on belly).

items.name: Abalone porridge
items.summary: Silky rice porridge with abalone, often from haenyeo catch.
items.expect: A breakfast and lunch classic.
items.tip: Pair with a seafood hot pot.

items.name: Hallabong tangerines
items.summary: Sweet, knobbly tangerines sold fresh, as juice and in sweets.
items.expect: Dongmun Market has the most stalls.
items.tip: Try hallabong juice.

name: Okinawa · Naha
tagline: Ryukyu castles, coral seas and island food
summary: Okinawa was the independent Ryukyu Kingdom until 1879, and its culture still feels different from mainland Japan. Naha has the rebuilt Shuri Castle and the lively Kokusai-dōri, while the island has turquoise beaches, one of the world's largest aquariums and somber Second World War memorials.
seasonNote: March, April, October and November are warm and less humid. The rainy season runs from May to June; July to September is hot, with typhoons. Winter is mild but too cool for swimming.
arrival: Fly to Naha Airport from Tokyo (about 2.5 hours), Osaka, Fukuoka, Seoul or Taipei. The Yui Rail monorail runs to the city centre.
gettingAround: The monorail covers Naha; rent a car for the rest of the island, as buses are slow.
cashTip: Cards are increasingly accepted, but carry yen for small restaurants and markets.
foodTip: Okinawa soba, goya champuru, taco rice, sea grapes and Orion beer.
buyTip: Ryukyu glass, Tsuboya pottery, shisa lion figures and brown sugar sweets.

items.name: Shuri Castle
items.summary: The red palace of the Ryukyu kings on a hill over Naha, being rebuilt after a 2019 fire.
items.expect: Grounds, gates and the reconstruction site are open to visit.
items.tip: Watch the rebuilding through the viewing windows.

items.name: Kokusai-dōri
items.summary: Naha's busy main street of shops, bars and restaurants.
items.expect: Car-free on Sunday afternoons.
items.tip: Duck into the side arcades and the public market.

items.name: Tsuboya pottery street
items.summary: A quiet lane of pottery kilns and shops near the market.
items.expect: Small museum and workshops.
items.tip: Buy a shisa lion as a souvenir.
items.why: Okinawa crafts in an old neighbourhood.

items.name: Sēfa-utaki
items.summary: The holiest site of the Ryukyu faith, a rock shrine in a forest.
items.expect: A short walk through the woods.
items.tip: Look through the triangular rock gap to Kudaka Island.

items.name: Okinawa Peace Memorial Park
items.summary: Memorials to the more than 200,000 who died in the Battle of Okinawa.
items.expect: A museum and walls of names by the sea.
items.tip: Visit the Himeyuri memorial nearby.

items.name: Churaumi Aquarium
items.summary: A giant tank with whale sharks and manta rays.
items.expect: About two hours' drive north of Naha.
items.tip: Combine with Emerald Beach next door.
items.why: One of the world's great aquariums.

items.name: Kerama Islands
items.summary: A national park of white beaches and clear water, with sea turtles.
items.expect: Ferries from Naha take 35 to 70 minutes.
items.tip: Stay a night on Tokashiki or Zamami.

items.name: Okinawa soba
items.summary: Thick wheat noodles in pork broth with soft-braised pork rib.
items.expect: Every town has its favourite shop.
items.tip: Add a splash of koregusu chilli spirit.

items.name: Goya champuru
items.summary: Stir-fried bitter melon with tofu, egg and pork.
items.expect: On every izakaya menu.
items.tip: Try it with Orion beer.
items.why: The taste of Okinawa's long-life diet.

items.name: Taco rice
items.summary: Taco filling on rice, born near the US bases.
items.expect: Cheap and filling.
items.tip: Try it at its birthplace in Kin.
